zenodo.title: Database for the surveillance of non-EU Cicadomorpha, vectors of Xylella fastidiosa, in the EU
zenodo.abstract:
This database was prepared in the context of the EFSA mandate on plant pest surveillance (M-2020-0114), at the request of the European Commission. 

It provides open access to the available information on life cycle, native range, climate suitability, host plants, spread capacity and detection and identification methods of 48 non-EU Cicadomorpha taxa, known to be vectors of Xylella fastidiosa (Wells et al.), regulated as Union quarantine pests in Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2019/2072.

zenodo.title: Scientific opinion on the distribution of hoppers (Hemiptera: cicadomorpha & Fulgoromorpha) on cereal crops and sunflower in Bulgaria – potential vectors of the regulated pathogen Xylella fastidiosa
zenodo.abstract: Information on the species composition and abundance of hoppers (spittlebugs, leafhoppers, plant hoppers) on wheat, barley, triticale, corn and sunflower in three Bulgarian regions (Southwestern, Southeastern and Central Northern) was analyzed. In total, 55 hoppers species of six families were identified, of which 21 were pests on the respective crops. The hopper species established on each crop were classified in two groups - harmful and indifferent; then the group of harmful species was further split into permanent and non-permanent inhabitants. zenodo.title: Efficiency of different trap types for the monitoring of Philaenus spumarius
zenodo.abstract: The spittlebug Philaenus spumarius (Cicadomorpha: Aphrophoridae) is the principal vector of Xylella fastidiosa in Europe. Surveys on the occurrence and abundance of this and other spittlebug species are necessary for the identification of endangered crops and natural refugia, risk assessment, the development of prevention strategies, or decision support regarding control measures. zenodo.title: Relative efficacy of different colour sticky traps for the capture of vectors of Xylella fastidiosa
zenodo.abstract: Xylella fastidiosa is one of the main quarantine pathogens of the European Union that is transmitted by xylem-feeder insects (i.e. Cicadomorpha). This bacterium affects plant species of great economic importance such as almond, olive , and vine, among others. During 2020 we conducted a trial in Mallorca (Balearic Islands; Spain) to study the efficacy of colour sticky traps to capture spittle bugs (Aphrophoridae) which are considered major vectors of X. fastidiosa in the EU. zenodo.title: Identification and monitoring of Xylella fastidiosa potential vectors on modern olive orchard
zenodo.abstract: The knowledge of Xylella fastidiosa potential vectors is important for control the spread of the disease. Until now, in Europe, have been identified, as potential vectors of X. fastidiosa, insects belong to two large families. Philaenus spumarius and Neophilaenus campestris are the main X. fastidiosa vectors from Aphrophoridae family.
